svg.title: What would you like to do for Halloween?

text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/10/31 - Small talk - 01

svg.title: Pumpkin carving offers a quieter alternative to a haunted attraction.

text.tspan: Pumpkin carving offers a quieter alternative to a haunted attraction.
What would you like to do for
Halloween?
An open invitation to share Halloween preferences
without assuming that the other person celebrates it.
“What would you like to do for Halloween—if you’re doing
anything this year?”
Offer a low-pressure follow-up. If someone says they do
not celebrate, accept the answer and move to another
topic rather than asking them to justify it.
A: What would you like to do for Halloween, if you’re
doing anything this year?
B: Something low-key. I’m not really into haunted
houses.
A: Same here. How about carving a pumpkin and making
dinner?
B: That sounds more like me. Have you ever managed
one of those elaborate designs?
A: Once. It looked impressive for about ten minutes
before it collapsed.
B: Then let’s start with a face we can actually finish.
Your neighbor replies, “I don’t celebrate Halloween,
actually.” Write a friendly response that acknowledges
this and smoothly opens a different topic.
